details:
MAST — Martian Analysis of Situational Topography

An interactive Mars mission-planning platform

1. What it does and how it works

MAST is a Mars mission-planning prototype that allows users to explore Martian terrain, plan rover routes, and evaluate obstacles using real planetary data.

Users can create private missions, explore Mars through a NASA Viking-based 2D map and a 3D globe, define mandatory waypoints, and manually mark and confirm obstacles.

MAST calculates routes around confirmed obstacles while preserving waypoint order. If no valid route exists, it reports the failure instead of guessing. Users can also create new drafts without modifying saved routes.

Jezero Crater: Real-world comparison

MAST compares its suggested route with Perseverance's actual traverse between corresponding stops.

Approximately 63% of the combined paths lie within 50 metres of each other.

It also features a high-resolution HiRISE terrain layer specifically for Jezero Crater.

To enable it: Select Jezero Initial Mission → Terrains → Mapped Units and Colour Image — Jezero Only → HiRISE.

2. Benefits and intended impact

A straight line on a map is not a mission plan.

MAST aims to make planetary route planning easier to explore and understand for students, early-career teams, and space enthusiasts.

It keeps evidence, uncertainty, and data sources visible throughout the planning process.

3. Tools and technology

  • Frontend: TypeScript, React, Vite, Leaflet and Three.js.
  • Backend: Express 5, PostgreSQL and Drizzle ORM.
  • Authentication: Clerk.
  • Validation: OpenAPI and Zod.
  • Machine Learning: TensorFlow.js.
  • Voice: Opt-in browser-based assistant with predefined actions.
  • Platform: Built and hosted on Replit.

Data sources: NASA/JPL Mars Trek, MOLA elevation, USGS HiRISE maps, Perseverance imagery and AI4Mars labels (CC BY 4.0).

No specialised hardware is required. MAST runs in a browser.

4. What makes it different?

  • Operator-confirmed obstacles: Users verify obstacle positions and dimensions rather than relying on unverified automatic detection.
  • Real rover comparison: Evaluates suggested routes against Perseverance's actual traverse.
  • Transparent limitations: MAST is not an autonomous driving, hazard detection, telemetry or certified risk-assessment system.
  • Additional features: Guided tour, keyboard shortcuts, command console, voice assistant and invite-only team collaboration.

5. Responsible development and limitations

The experimental terrain-scoring model achieved 25.3% held-out accuracy against a 25% chance baseline. It is therefore labelled experimental and is not presented as a risk measurement.

Elevation scores with incompatible quality data are withheld. Missions remain private, voice is opt-in, and data licences and credits are provided in-app.

Future development: Improved model evaluation, verified depth and georeferencing, vehicle-specific constraints and real-world validation.

6. AI Tools Used

  • ChatGPT
  • Replit Agents

Before exploring MAST

  1. Complete the guided tour to understand the application's workflow.
  2. Check your initial missions: A freshly registered account should contain two initial projects. If one is missing, execute version --upgrade in the in-app terminal. It should complete in under five seconds.
  3. Visit the Credits tab for complete data-source attribution and licensing.
  4. Explore Jezero: Enable the HiRISE layer under the Terrains tab for high-resolution terrain exploration.
